Select function (only show 15 rows, rather than the whole dataset)


```{r select_function}
crab_data <- pie_crab %>%
  slice(round(seq(1, n(), length.out = 15))) %>%
  select(date, site, latitude, size, air_temp, water_temp)

col_options <- c("none", names(crab_data))

choices <- expand.grid(
  col1 = col_options, 
  col2 = col_options, 
  col3 = col_options,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

make_code <- function(col1, col2, col3) {
  cols <- unique(c(col1, col2, col3))
  cols <- cols[cols != "none"]
  if (length(cols) == 0) return("crab_data")
  paste0("crab_data %>%\n  select(", paste(cols, collapse = ", "), ")")
}

choices$code <- mapply(make_code, choices$col1, choices$col2, choices$col3,
                       USE.NAMES = FALSE)
results <- lapply(choices$code, function(code) eval(parse(text = code)))

choices$before <- vapply(results, function(r) {
  kept <- names(crab_data) %in% names(r)
  html_table(crab_data, col_class = ifelse(kept, "kept-col", "dropped-col"))
}, character(1))

choices$after <- vapply(results, function(r) html_table(r), character(1))

ojs_define(choices = choices, 
           col_options = col_options)
```

```{ojs select_func_input1}
viewof col1 = Inputs.select(col_options, {label: "Column 1"})
```

```{ojs select_func_input2}
viewof col2 = Inputs.select(col_options, {label: "Column 2"})
```

```{ojs select_func_input3}
viewof col3 = Inputs.select(col_options, {label: "Column 3"})
```

```{ojs select_func_input4}
//| output: false
rows = transpose(choices)
match = rows.find(d => d.col1 === col1 && d.col2 === col2 && d.col3 === col3)
```

```{ojs select_func_display}
{
  const pre = document.createElement("pre");
  pre.className = "plot-code";
  const code = document.createElement("code");
  code.textContent = match.code;
  pre.appendChild(code);
  return pre;
}
```

```{ojs select_func_display2}
{
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.className = "side-by-side";
  wrap.innerHTML =
    "<div><p><b>Before</b></p>" + match.before + "</div>" +
    "<div><p><b>After</b></p>" + match.after + "</div>";
  return wrap;
}
```

let's try this

```{r filter_func}
crab_data <- pie_crab %>% 
  slice(round(seq(1, n(), length.out = 20))) %>% 
  mutate(row = row_number(), .before = 1) %>% 
  select(row, date, site, latitude, size, air_temp)

site_options <- c("any", sort(unique(as.character(crab_data$site))))
size_options <- c(0, 15, 20, 25)

choices2 <- expand.grid(
  site = site_options,
  size = size_options, 
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

make_code_filter <- function(site, size){
  conditions <- c(
    if(site != "any") paste0('site == "', site, '"'),
    if(size > 0) paste0('size >= ', size)
  )
  if(length(conditions) == 0) return("crab_data")
  paste0("crab_data %>%\n filter(", paste(conditions, collapse = ", "), ")")
}

choices2$code <- mapply(make_code_filter, choices2$site, choices2$size,
                        USE.NAMES = FALSE)

results2 <- lapply(choices2$code, function(code) eval(parse(text = code)))

choices2$before <- vapply(results2, function(r) {
  kept <- crab_data$row %in% r$row
  html_table(select(crab_data, -row), row_class = ifelse(kept, "kept", "dropped"))
}, character(1))

choices2$after <- vapply(results2, function(r) {
  html_table(select(r, -row))
}, character(1))

ojs_define(choices2 = choices2,
           site_options = site_options,
           size_options = size_options)
```

```{ojs filter_func_input1}
viewof site2 = Inputs.select(site_options, {label: "Site"})
```

```{ojs filter_func_input2}
viewof min_size2 = Inputs.select(size_options, {label: "Minimum size"})
```

```{ojs filter_func_input3}
//| output: false
rows2 = transpose(choices2)
match2 = rows2.find(d => d.site === site2 && d.size === min_size2)
```

```{ojs filter_func_display1}
{
  const pre = document.createElement("pre");
  pre.className = "plot-code";
  const code = document.createElement("code");
  code.textContent = match2.code;
  pre.appendChild(code);
  return pre;
}
```

```{ojs filter_func_display2}
{
  const wrap = document.createElement("div");
  wrap.className = "side-by-side";
  wrap.innerHTML =
    "<div><p><b>Before</b></p>" + match2.before + "</div>" +
    "<div><p><b>After</b></p>" + match2.after + "</div>";
  return wrap;
}
```

`geom_point()` draws one dot per row of your data. Choose which columns go on each axis and optionally colour the dots by a third column.

```{r create_plot_r}
crab_data <- pie_crab %>% 
  select(site, latitude, size, air_temp, water_temp)

variables <- sort(unique(as.character(names(crab_data))))

choices3 <- expand.grid(
  x = c(variables),
  y = c(variables),
  color = c(variables),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) %>% 
  filter(x != y)

axis_names <- c(
  size = "Size", 
  air_temp = "Air Temperature",
  water_temp = "Water Temperature",
  latitude = "Latitude",
  site = "Site")

nice <- function(v) if (v %in% names(axis_names)) axis_names[[v]] else v

make_code_plot <- function(x, y, color) {
  aes_txt <- paste0("x = ", x, ", y = ", y)
  if (color != "none") aes_txt <- paste0(aes_txt, ", color = ", color)

  labs_lines <- c(
    paste0('x = "', nice(x), '"'),
    paste0('y = "', nice(y), '"')
  )
  if (color != "none") {
    labs_lines <- c(labs_lines, paste0('color = "', nice(color), '"'))
  }
  labs_txt <- paste0("    ", labs_lines, collapse = ",\n")

  paste0(
    "crab_data %>%\n",
    "  ggplot(aes(", aes_txt, ")) +\n",
    "  geom_point() +\n",
    "  labs(\n", labs_txt, ") +\n",
    "  theme_bw()"
  )
}

choices3$code <- mapply(make_code_plot, 
                       choices3$x, 
                       choices3$y, 
                       choices3$color,
                       USE.NAMES = FALSE)

choices3$image <- vapply(choices3$code, function(code) {
  plot_to_uri(eval(parse(text = code)))
  }, 
  character(1), USE.NAMES = FALSE)

ojs_define(choices3 = choices3,
           variables = variables)
```

```{ojs dropdown_x}
viewof x = Inputs.select(variables, {label: "X axis"})
```

```{ojs dropdown_y}
viewof y = Inputs.select(variables, {label: "Y axis"})
```

```{ojs dropdown_color}
viewof color = Inputs.select(variables, {label: "Colour by"})
```

```{ojs transpose}
//| output: false
rows3 = transpose(choices3)
match3 = rows3.find(d => d.x === x && d.y === y && d.color === color)
```

```{ojs prevent_same_dropdowns}
{
if (!match3) {
const p = document.createElement("p");
p.textContent = "Pick two different columns for X and Y.";
return p;
}
const img = document.createElement("img");
img.src = match3.image;
img.style.maxWidth = "100%";
return img;
}
```

The code that made this plot:

```{ojs display_code}
{
const pre = document.createElement("pre");
pre.className = "plot-code";
const code = document.createElement("code");
code.textContent = match3 ? match3.code : "";
pre.appendChild(code);
return pre;
}
```
